text:
jordan lee: hi team, first day issue: trying to clone git.internal.redwood and it hangs on name lookup. ping git.internal.redwood times out, but `nslookup git.internal.redwood 10.12.3.9` returns correct IP. i'm on Windows 11 WSL2 distro. any tips?

tayla s: welcome! sounds like WSL is using Windows DNS, which might not get split-tunnel routes. from WSL, what's `cat /etc/resolv.conf` show and `ip route`? also are you using the corp vpn client on the host or WSL?

jordan lee: host shows vpn connected. /etc/resolv.conf in WSL has nameserver 172.22.0.1 (WSL internal) and windows host has 10.12.3.9 for internal domains. ip route is default via vEthernet (WSL).

ben r: WSL sometimes proxies DNS to the Windows host. If the host resolver isn't reachable for that suffix, update WSL's /etc/resolv.conf or disable auto generation and write 10.12.3.9 directly. Steps: `sudo rm /etc/resolv.conf && echo "nameserver 10.12.3.9" | sudo tee /etc/resolv.conf` and then try `sudo systemctl restart systemd-resolved` (if systemd).

jordan lee: i can't restart systemd (WSL distro doesn't use systemd). i replaced resolv.conf and now `ping` resolves but git clone still stalls during TLS handshake (stuck at "TLS handshake").

tayla s: TLS hang might be because traffic to the git host is routed via host but not allowed through split-tunnel for that source port. can you `curl -v https://git.internal.redwood` from WSL and paste the headers/logs? also check Windows firewall or corporate endpoint agent blocking WSL processes.

jordan lee: curl -v shows connected then nothing: "* Connected to git.internal.redwood (10.12.3.45) port 443 (#0)" then stalls. On host (powershell) curl works fine.

ben r: sounds like Windows-side packet forwarding for WSL isn't handling the encrypted handshake properly over the VPN. Two options: 1) run git from Windows (not WSL), or 2) enable "Expose DNS to WSL" in Windows’ WSL settings and make sure the VPN client allows the WSL subnet. For quick unblock, run `git clone` in powershell.

netops-bot: Route record: added route 10.12.0.0/16 via wg-host-1 at 2067000105 for user jordan.

jordan lee: cloned from powershell, works. i'll follow up with IT to allow WSL traffic or ask for a proxy entry. thanks everyone!

tayla s: i'll add a note to onboarding: "Windows WSL users: if internal hosts resolve on host but not in WSL, either update /etc/resolv.conf in WSL or run networking actions through the host; if TLS handshakes stall, use host-native git or request WSL-compatible routing from infra." tagging infra to evaluate.

ben r: follow-up: infra will try to include WSL subnet in VPN split-rules; @netops-bot please create ticket.

netops-bot: Ticket created: NETOPS-4721 for WSL routing support at 2067000225.

jordan lee: huge help, peace of mind for my first day :relieved:
